questions.question: What does the logical date of a scheduled DAG run normally identify?
options: The start of the run's data interval
The wall-clock instant when the first worker starts
The time when the DAG file was last edited
The deadline for every task
questions.explanation: For a scheduled run, the logical date identifies the beginning of its data interval; execution usually starts after that interval has ended.

questions.question: A newly enabled daily DAG has three missing historical intervals, but catchup is disabled. What should the scheduler create?
options: Only the latest scheduled interval
All three missing intervals
A single run covering all three days
No run until a backfill is created
questions.explanation: With catchup disabled, the scheduler does not automatically create every missed scheduled run; it creates the latest interval.

questions.question: Why should a backfill usually start with a small maximum-active-runs value?
options: To protect warehouses, APIs, and other dependencies from a sudden historical workload
To stop Airflow from recording task history
To combine all intervals into one task instance
To disable retries during the backfill
questions.explanation: Historical runs can multiply ordinary task traffic. A bounded concurrency limit lets operators observe downstream pressure before increasing parallelism.

questions.question: A target commits a write, but the acknowledgement is lost and Airflow retries the task. What prevents duplicate output?
options: An interval-scoped idempotency or merge key
A larger retry count
A shorter scheduler heartbeat
Storing the full dataset in XCom
questions.explanation: Airflow cannot infer whether an ambiguous external write committed. The target operation must recognize replay of the same logical interval.

questions.question: Which failure should normally fail fast instead of consuming the full retry budget?
options: An invalid service credential
A brief network reset
A warehouse restarting for one minute
A rate limit with a known reset time
questions.explanation: Time alone does not repair a deterministic authentication error. Repeating it delays diagnosis and consumes capacity.

questions.question: What is an appropriate value to pass through XCom?
options: The object-storage URI of a completed partition
A multi-gigabyte transformed dataset
An entire warehouse table snapshot
A long-lived plaintext service credential
questions.explanation: XCom is for small coordination values. Large data belongs in durable data systems, while secrets belong in managed connections or secret backends.
